mcqs.q: Across the meta-analysis of free-ranging felids, T. gondii oocyst shedding prevalence was positively associated with which factor?
o: Human population density at the sampling location
mcqs.e: Shedding rose with human population density in both domestic cats and wild felids.

mcqs.q: Which intervention did the authors propose to reduce environmental T. gondii oocyst burden?
mcqs.e: Domestic cats' large populations and affinity for human settlements make their management a key lever.

mcqs.q: What life stage shed by felids is responsible for most environmental T. gondii contamination?
mcqs.e: Felids, the definitive hosts, shed environmentally resistant oocysts in feces.

mcqs.q: Which tick species was the vector of concern for the pathogens studied in sheltered border dogs?
mcqs.e: The study targeted pathogens vectored by brown dog ticks.

mcqs.q: A key clinical-relevance warning for clinicians was that Rocky Mountain spotted fever may co-occur with which infections?
mcqs.e: The authors warned that E. canis or A. platys infection may co-occur with R. rickettsii.

mcqs.q: Which finding best supports the One Health public-health concern raised by the study?
o: Only Mexican shelters showed any exposure
Dogs in all four locations showed exposure to all three pathogens
mcqs.e: Exposure to all three pathogens occurred across all sites, signaling spread potential with human health consequences.

mcqs.q: What proportion of UK and Ireland parks sampled contained Toxocara-type eggs?
mcqs.e: Characteristic Toxocara eggs were found in 86.6% of parks.

mcqs.q: Egg density and positivity were highest in parks with which characteristic?
mcqs.e: Positive samples and egg density rose with greater perceived dog fouling.

mcqs.q: Which species was confirmed by sequencing, and were many eggs viable?
o: Toxocara canis; many contained developed larvae and were potentially infective
mcqs.e: Eggs were confirmed as T. canis, many with developed larvae and thus potentially infective.

authors: Georgios Sioutas, Elias Papadopoulos, Maxime Madder, Frederic Beugnet, Eric Tielemans

mcqs.q: By Day 45, what reduction in live Otodectes cynotis counts did afoxolaner-treated dogs achieve versus untreated controls?
mcqs.e: Single or two-dose afoxolaner regimens produced a 99.9% reduction in live mite counts.

mcqs.q: What did the trial conclude about a single oral dose of afoxolaner for ear mites?
o: It was effective, achieving near-complete mite reduction
mcqs.e: Even a single dose achieved 99.9% reduction, supporting afoxolaner-based treatment.

mcqs.q: How did clinical signs differ between treated and untreated dogs over the study?
o: Treated dogs improved while untreated dogs worsened
mcqs.e: Treated dogs showed reduced cerumen/debris while untreated dogs worsened.

authors: Siobhon Egan, Amanda D. Barbosa, Yaoyu Feng, Lihua Xiao, Una Ryan

mcqs.q: Which Cryptosporidium species dominates in rabbits and uniquely caused a 2008 UK waterborne outbreak?
mcqs.e: C. cuniculus is the dominant rabbit species and the only one besides C. hominis/C. parvum to cause a waterborne outbreak.

mcqs.q: Despite rabbit abundance, how common are human C. cuniculus reports overall?
o: Relatively rare except in the UK and New Zealand
More common than C. parvum globally
mcqs.e: Human reports are relatively rare except in the UK and New Zealand.

mcqs.q: Which Giardia duodenalis assemblage dominated in rabbits in the reviewed studies?
mcqs.e: Assemblage B dominated among the limited rabbit Giardia studies.

authors: Simona Gabrielli, Giovanni Luigi Milardi, Ludovica Scarinci, Caterina Fanì, Michele Trotta

mcqs.q: Which method is the reference standard for diagnosing Giardia in canine fecal samples?
mcqs.e: DFA is cited as the reference standard for laboratory Giardia diagnosis in dogs.

mcqs.q: How did PCR perform for detecting Giardia in this study, and what was its main added value?
o: Low sensitivity; but identified zoonotic assemblage B
Equal to DFA; identified only dog-specific assemblages
mcqs.e: PCR detection performance was low but it identified the zoonotic B assemblage in 25% of positives.

mcqs.q: What public-health implication did the 26% DFA prevalence and zoonotic assemblages suggest?
o: Frequent cross-species transmission between dogs and humans
Only immunocompromised cats are at risk
mcqs.e: Finding zoonotic assemblages indicates potential public-health risk and cross-species transmission.

mcqs.q: What treatment did the study recommend for sheltered dogs with triple blood pathogen infection (Babesia vogeli, Ehrlichia canis, Anaplasma platys)?
mcqs.e: The authors proposed 28-day doxycycline monotherapy to clear all pathogens.

mcqs.q: Which hematologic abnormalities were most common in the triple-infected dogs?
mcqs.e: Most dogs showed anemia and thrombocytopenia.

mcqs.q: By what day were all pathogens cleared by PCR after starting doxycycline?
mcqs.e: Pathogens were undetectable by day 14 and fully cleared by day 28.

mcqs.q: Against Ancylostoma caninum, which treatment had the poorest efficacy in this trial?
mcqs.e: Oxibendazole cleared only 9% of dogs, making it inept against A. caninum.

mcqs.q: Why was off-label ivermectin deemed unsuitable in this program?
o: It had poor efficacy against ectoparasites
mcqs.e: Ivermectin eliminated 0% of ectoparasite infestations, unsuitable for that purpose.

mcqs.q: Which agents appeared suitable for ectoparasite control?
mcqs.e: Afoxolaner and imidacloprid/flumethrin collars effectively eliminated ectoparasites.

mcqs.q: What was the overall T. gondii seroprevalence among the symptomatic cats living with women of childbearing age?
mcqs.e: 31 of 150 cats (20.7%) were seropositive overall.

mcqs.q: Which clinical signs were significantly associated with IgM-only (recent/active) positivity?
mcqs.e: Neurological and ocular signs were significantly associated with IgM-only positivity.

mcqs.q: What public-health conclusion did the authors draw?
o: Cats pose no toxoplasmosis risk to households
Cats with women of childbearing age are at risk and awareness should stay high
mcqs.e: The study concluded these cats are at risk and toxoplasmosis awareness should remain high to protect public health.

mcqs.q: What was the conclusion regarding oral lotilaner for Otodectes cynotis in ferrets?
o: Effective only with two extra doses
mcqs.e: Lotilaner was a safe, efficient, easy, and satisfactory treatment with no adverse effects.

mcqs.q: By Day 28 after lotilaner dosing, what were the mean adult/nymph mite counts in the ferrets?
mcqs.e: Mean adult/nymph counts fell from 11.2 at D0 to 0 at D28.

mcqs.q: How did quality-of-life scores change by Day 56?
mcqs.e: Mean QoL impact dropped significantly from 4.5/18 at D0 to 0 at D56.

mcqs.q: In dogs, which Leptospira serogroup had significantly higher seroprevalence than other pathogenic serogroups?
mcqs.e: L. interrogans serogroup Canicola prevalence was significantly higher in dogs.

mcqs.q: What role can asymptomatic domestic dogs and cats play regarding leptospires, per the review?
o: Reservoirs or sentinels of environmental contamination
mcqs.e: Pets may act as reservoirs or sentinels of environmental Leptospira contamination.

mcqs.q: Which serogroup was significantly more prevalent in stray/sheltered dogs than domiciled dogs?
mcqs.e: Moderator analysis showed Grippotyphosa was higher in stray/sheltered dogs.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about the reliability of the Feline Grimace Scale across different rater groups?
o: Reliable when used by individuals with different experience levels
mcqs.e: The FGS showed good inter-rater reliability and very good agreement with veterinarians across owners, students, and nurses.

mcqs.q: Which FGS facial action units yielded the lowest reliability?
mcqs.e: Muzzle and whiskers had lower reliability (ICC 0.39 to 0.74).

mcqs.q: Which rater characteristic significantly affected FGS scores?
mcqs.e: Female raters assigned higher scores; age and number of cats owned had no effect.
